svg.title: The rows and the cursor commit together, or not at all
svg.desc: A whiteboard sketch showing three pagination styles with offset pagination crossed out in red because rows shift between pages; an exponential backoff timeline with marks at one, two, four and eight seconds plus dashed jitter marks; the central idea drawn as one green box containing both the thousand fetched rows and the cursor value 43000 with a single commit arrow leaving it, and the two alternative orderings struck through as causing duplicates or data loss; and a progress bar to a hundred thousand records with a crash marked at forty-three thousand, annotated that resuming took exactly one hundred API calls in total, the same as an uninterrupted run, with matching checksums.
svg.text: The rows and the cursor commit together, or not at all
three ways to walk a paged API
you saw one row twice and missed another. No error.
a cursor is a POSITION IN THE DATA, not a position in a list
without jitter every client retries in lockstep
and DDoSes the source the moment it recovers
and read the Retry-After header if the API
sends one. Your backoff is a guess; that
THE ONE THING THAT MAKES IT RESUMABLE
rows, THEN cursor -> crash between = duplicates
cursor, THEN rows -> crash between = DATA LOSS
the actual test: kill it at 43,000
after the crash: 43,000 rows, cursor = 43000, 43 API calls
100 API calls in total - identical to a clean run
and the checksums matched: sum = 14,999,850,000, count = 100,000
...now do it for a source with no cursor at all
